title: Methi Chicken
subtitle: Boneless chicken thighs cooked with dried fenugreek and warm spices
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs cooked in a thick onion and tomato masala, finished with a generous handful of dried fenugreek leaves. The methi gives the sauce a slightly bitter, herbal depth that balances the richness.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian restaurant staple combining dried methi (fenugreek leaf) with a standard masala base.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently, adding a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wide, deep pan so the chicken pieces are not overcrowded.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The flavour improves overnight. Make a day ahead and reheat over a low heat.

content.text: Methi chicken is built on a slow-cooked onion base that must be properly golden before the tomatoes go in. The dried fenugreek leaves go in at the very end so their flavour stays bright. Do not swap dried methi for fresh as the flavour is different.

items.prepNote: dried, rubbed between palms before using

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 15 minutes until deep golden brown. Stir every few minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger. Fry for 2 minutes, stirring constantly so nothing burns.
Add the turmeric, cumin, coriander, and chilli powder. Stir for 1 minute to cook the spices in the oil.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Crush them with the spoon. Cook on a medium heat for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and oil begins to separate at the edges.
Add the chicken pieces and salt. Stir well to coat in the masala. Cook for 5 minutes on a high heat to seal the chicken.
Reduce to a medium-low heat. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the lid. Stir in the garam masala and dried fenugreek leaves. Cook for 2 minutes more. Taste and adjust salt. Scatter with fresh coriander if using.

items.cause: The tomatoes were not cooked down long enough before adding the chicken.
items.fix: Remove the lid and cook on a medium heat for a further 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce tightens.

items.symptom: The onion base is bitter and sharp.
items.cause: The onions were not cooked long enough and still taste raw.
items.fix: The onion stage needs a full 15 minutes. If in doubt, cook for 5 minutes more before continuing.

items.cause: Too much was used, or it was added early and cooked for too long.
items.fix: Start with 1 tablespoon next time and always add it in the final 2 minutes only.
